newsitem.title: USA: Anti-gun group blasts Virginia governor over veto.
newsitem.headline: Anti-gun group blasts Virginia governor over veto.

text.p: A major gun control group blasted Virginia Gov. George Allen Tuesday for vetoing a bill to bar guns from a county's youth recreation areas, but the National Rifle Association praised him and his understanding of gun laws.
Handgun Control Inc., founded by former presidential press secretary James Brady and his wife, Sarah, said the conservative Republican governor had given in to the gun lobby.

Allen Monday vetoed a measure that would have barred guns, knives and other weapons from teen centres or other recreation areas in Fairfax County, a Washington suburb, saying the legislation would not have made the county a safer place.
The action also outraged legislators who had promoted the measure as a way to prevent a recurrence of a series of gun-related events at recreation places.
Allen also vetoed a second measure that would have prohibited people other than police from carrying weapons into police stations in Fairfax County.

"Once again, the governor of Virginia has sacrificed our children's safety on the altar of the extreme leadership of the gun lobby," Sarah Brady said in a statement. "Like Pinocchio to Gepetto, George Allen has let the National Rifle Association pull his strings one more time," she said.
The National Rifle Association lobbied heavily against the two measures vetoed by Allen and Sarah Brady said Allen had often sided with the gun lobby over the last four years.

The NRA said it agreed with Allen that the proposed measures would not have prevented one crime. "Governor Allen has a much better understanding of how to fight crime than Sarah Brady ever had," NRA official Chip Walker said of the Bradys' statement.

He pointed to Allen's record since taking office, including proposals to abolish parole and to make it easier for law abiding citizens to carry weapons for self-defence, and said the crime rate had gone down under Allen.
James Brady was seriously wounded and left partially paralysed in the attempted assassination of President Ronald Reagan in March 1981.
